newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower, silver leads.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower, silver leads.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower Tuesday, with fund and trade selling, taking the complex down to two year lows in December silver.
"We saw every type of selling today - fund selling, trade selling, producer hedging, and locals selling on weak looking technicals," Credit Suisse New York vice president, Ian MacDonald said.
"Spot gold still looks like it has support around $380, but it's hard to say where silver is going," he said.
COMEX December silver ended down 11.0 cents at $4.820 an ounce, after seeing a session low at $4.810, the lowest level since late 1994. Estimated silver volume was 21,000 lots.
Spot silver fell to a low around $4.82 an ounce, not far from the 18 month low at $4.81 seen in late September.
The spot gold/silver ratio widened to a new 18 month high at 79.07 at the close, as silver weakened faster than gold.
COMEX December gold ended down $3.00 an ounce at $381.60, after seeing an intraday low at $381.50, testing last week's support level. Estimated gold futures volume was 55,000 lots.
Spot gold bullion ended quoted $380.35/380.85, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $381.70 and the New York close Monday at $382.90/383.40.
Key support is still seen around $380 in spot gold, the level which has held several times in the past 18 months, apart from a brief dip to $376.90 in early October.
Last week both silver and gold recovered to two week highs, on fund shortcovering, but the longer term downtrend in place for most of the year still looks intact, analysts said.
While the monthly OTC options expiry occurred Tuesday, traders said it produced little impact.

However, a large rally in U.S. bond markets, after bullish third quarter employment cost data and a fall in October consumer confidence, accompanied by a strong stock market, discouraged investors in precious metals, traders said.
"The breakout in the U.S. 30 year bond futures to multi-month highs encouraged more fund selling," Friedberg Mercantile Group's Toronto-based trader Jeff Kowal said.
Unconfirmed rumors of further European central bank selling of gold reserves, as EU countries seek to meet the 1999 single-currency criteria, depressed sentiment also.
End-of-year producer hedging was also a factor, traders said, with the 12-month December 1996/December 1997 contango falling below $14.00 this week for the first time in nine months.
The fall in the South African rand to to a record low 4.6940 against the dollar Tuesday was unnerving South African gold producers, analysts said.
While the weak rand/dollar increased returns on dollar priced assets, it was pushing up local South African costs and inflation, traders said.
Japanese demand for precious metals is also seen being undermined by the strength of the U.S. dollar, which hit a 42 month high against the yen Monday.
Japanese gold imports fell to 105 tonnes in the first eight months of 1996, down 47 percent on the same period last year, analysts noted.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $4.70 at $383.80 an ounce, after seeing a fresh life-of-contract low at $383.10.
The April gold/April platinum intermarket spread has narrowed two-and-a-half year lows also this week, with the price of platinum falling to equal the price of gold.
In the bullion market, spot platinum fell to fresh three year lows around $379.20.
NYMEX December palladium ended down $1.55 at $116.25, after seeing a life-of-contract low at $116.00.
Spot palladium saw a low around $114.50, testing the three year low at $114.35 seen on October 17.
Platinum group metals have been under pressure from continued Russian selling on any price bounce and reductions in inventory by Japanese jewellers and electronics manufacturers, analsysts said.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
